claims.title: Posterior hidden-law belief is an exact sufficient state for Bayesian coding control
claims.scope: finite rational hidden Markov source-law models with action-independent hidden transitions and observation channels, finite zero-error prefix-codebook actions, and additive switching cost
assumptions: the hidden-state transition and current observation channel are known exactly
stage expected code length depends on history only through the current hidden source-law scenario and selected codebook
switching cost depends on history only through the previous and current codebooks
nonclaims: the belief vector is not asserted to be universally minimal under other observation or control architectures
a Bayesian sufficient state is not a parent-substrate memory claim

claims.title: Bayesian source-law information obeys the clairvoyant-perfect-observed-none cost hierarchy
claims.scope: the declared finite hidden Markov coding model under expected cumulative prefix length plus switching cost
assumptions: perfect current-state observation can simulate the declared noisy observation policy
a noisy-observation policy may ignore its signal
the path-first oracle selects a code sequence after observing the complete hidden-state path
nonclaims: the path-first oracle is a retrospective benchmark rather than an implementable causal policy
the hierarchy is for one known stochastic model rather than adversarial ambiguity

claims.title: An uninformative signal has zero value in the Bayesian expected-cost coding problem
claims.scope: the declared hidden-law model when every observation-channel row is identical
assumptions: the signal is independent of the hidden state
the objective is one fixed Bayesian expected cumulative cost
all exogenous random bits may be sampled before the horizon to represent a mixture over deterministic policy trees
nonclaims: uninformative public randomization can still help in a minimax game
the theorem does not deny the value of signals statistically dependent on the hidden state

claims.title: Dynamic Blackwell garbling cannot improve Bayesian coding value
claims.scope: two finite rational observation channels on the same action-independent hidden Markov source-law model when the poorer channel is a row-stochastic garbling of the richer channel
assumptions: the richer-signal policy may privately simulate the declared garbling kernel
hidden transitions and signal generation do not depend on the selected codebook
the objective is expected cumulative cost
nonclaims: Blackwell ordering is not a universal scalar ordering of channels outside the declared decision problem
action-dependent experiments require a different theorem

claims.title: Bayes regret against the path oracle differs from Bayes cost by one policy-independent constant
claims.scope: any policy class under the declared stochastic hidden-state path law and the same path-specific clairvoyant code-sequence oracle
assumptions: the path oracle depends on the hidden path but not on the policy's private randomization or observations
expectations are finite
nonclaims: the equivalence does not hold for minimax pathwise regret by subtracting separately optimized robust values
the oracle remains a benchmark rather than a causal policy

claims.title: Identity observation equals perfect current-state information and free switching removes future-foresight regret
claims.scope: the declared hidden-law model with an identity observation channel; the free-switching conclusion uses zero switching charge
assumptions: the identity signal reveals the current hidden scenario exactly
with zero switching charge the path oracle decomposes into independent periodwise codebook choices
nonclaims: perfect current-state information need not match clairvoyance when switching couples periods
identity of model signals is not an empirical claim about real observations

claims.title: Bayesian information and future foresight admit an exact nonnegative regret telescope
claims.scope: any valid belief-state coding certificate satisfying the declared information hierarchy
assumptions: all values use the same hidden Markov model, codebook family, horizon, switching charge, and path oracle
nonclaims: the additive terms are decision-value differences rather than Shannon mutual informations
the telescope does not price physical sensing or computation

claims.title: Finite-horizon hidden-law coding value is a piecewise-linear concave lower envelope in belief
claims.scope: finite hidden states, finite signal alphabet, finite prefix-codebook actions, finite horizon, rational transition and observation channels, and linear expected stage cost
assumptions: every deterministic policy tree is represented by its hidden-state conditional expected-cost alpha vector
the optimal cost is the minimum over the complete finite policy-tree alpha family
nonclaims: the exact alpha family is not asserted to be a minimal representation
policy-tree enumeration is bounded rather than a scalability result

claims.title: Posterior hidden-state belief and its one-step prediction satisfy exact martingale identities
claims.scope: one correctly specified finite observation channel and hidden-state transition applied to a rational prior belief
assumptions: conditioning is performed only on positive-probability signals
observation rows and transition rows are normalized
nonclaims: the martingale identity assumes the observation model is correctly specified
mean preservation does not imply that information has zero decision value

claims.title: Positive switching cost creates strict future-foresight value in a two-state K3 hidden-law model
claims.scope: the declared two hidden source laws, uniform redraw transition, horizon three, complete K3 confusion graph, and switching charge 2/5
assumptions: the bounded candidate enumeration returns the two nondominated source-specialized prefix trees
the hidden path follows the declared rational Markov model
nonclaims: the exact value 1/40 is specific to the declared instance
strict future-foresight value is not asserted for every positive switching charge

claims.title: Bounded exact belief filtering, alpha-vector, dynamic Blackwell, and hidden-path oracle audit
claims.scope: the finite rational hidden-law models, reachable beliefs, policy-tree alpha vectors, positive-probability paths, codebook candidates, and channel garblings exercised by the repository tests
assumptions: all configured hidden-path, alpha-vector, candidate, partition, and prefix-shape caps complete without truncation
Python Fraction arithmetic is used for every finite probability and cost calculation
nonclaims: bounded exact agreement is not an infinite-horizon or scalability theorem
finite Bayesian filtering results are not evidence that reality is simulated
